author: DamiLee
description:
Tolkien said all stories are about one thing. The answer changes everything you thought you knew about Middle-earth.

Men build monuments, carve cities into mountains, and march toward wars they know they cannot survive. That's not stubbornness. That's the whole point.

When Tolkien sketched Minas Tirith, he didn't draw the towering fortress we all picture. He drew something that looks more like a labyrinth. And in the Middle Ages, labyrinths weren't traps. They were guides. Pilgrims would walk them carved into cathedral floors, winding and turning, nearly losing hope, and then finally reaching the center.

A single continuous path. No dead ends. Just the long way round.

That's the paradox Tolkien buried inside the race of Men. They live knowing they will die, and they keep walking anyway. The mortality that feels like a curse turns out to be the engine behind everything they create, everywhere they build, every step they take toward a center they may never reach.

title: Minas Tirith Was Never a Fortress. It's a Labyrinth.
